title: Book Talk with Bruce Greenwald – Value Investing: From Graham to Buffett and Beyond
description: Bruce Greenwald, Robert Heilbrunn Professor Emeritus of Asset Management and Finance and Tano Santos, David L. and Elsie M. Dodd Professor of Finance and Faculty Director of the Heilbrunn Center discuss the Second Edition of “Value Investing: From Graham to Buffett and Beyond.”
summary: The talk argues that value investing relies on identifying companies that dominate specific, stable market segments where they can earn above-average returns, contrasting this with firms that operate in unstable or overly broad markets. It distinguishes between legacy industrial giants that dominated post-WWII but faced globalization, and modern technology firms that either specialize in niche areas or dominate entire industries like search and advertising. The core thesis is that investors should favor businesses with high barriers to entry, predictable growth, and customer captivity, while avoiding those in emerging markets with unstable technology or no customer lock-in.
